questions.question_text:
A circle has radius $7\text{ cm}$. A chord subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.
What is the exact perimeter of the minor segment?

options.why: Calculated only the arc length and omitted the chord.
Added two radii instead of the chord of length $7\text{ cm}$.
Used the diameter $14\text{ cm}$ instead of the radius when calculating the arc length.

questions.solution_text:
$l=r\theta=7\times\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{7\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$
The central triangle is equilateral, so the chord is $7\text{ cm}$.
$P=l+c=\dfrac{7\pi}{3}+7\text{ cm}$

questions.question_text:
A chord is perpendicular to a radius of a circle. The distance from the centre to the chord is $4\text{ cm}$, and the distance from the chord to the circle along the same radius is $4\text{ cm}$.
What is the exact area of the minor segment cut off by the chord?

options.why: Calculated the sector area and omitted subtraction of the triangle area.
Added the triangle area instead of subtracting it.
Used the half-angle $\pi/3$ instead of the full central angle $2\pi/3$ in both area calculations.

questions.question_text:
An annular sector has outer radius $9\text{ cm}$, inner radius $3\text{ cm}$ and central angle $90^{\circ}$.
Find its exact area.

options.why: Omitted the factor of $1/2$ in the area formula.
Squared the difference of the radii instead of subtracting their squares.
Calculated only the outer sector area without subtracting the inner sector.

questions.question_text:
A circle has a radius of $12\text{ cm}$.
What is the exact perimeter of the minor segment subtended by a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$?

options.why: Calculated the perimeter of the sector ($l + 2r$) instead of the segment ($l + \text{chord}$).
Calculated only the arc length without adding the chord length.
Halved the arc length during calculation.

questions.solution_text:
Arc length:
$l = r\theta = 12 \times \dfrac{\pi}{3} = 4\pi\text{ cm}$
Since $\Delta OAB$ is equilateral ($OA = OB = 12$ and angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$), chord $AB = 12\text{ cm}$.
$P = l + c$
$= 4\pi + 12\text{ cm}$

questions.question_text:
An annular sector is bounded by concentric circles of radii $6\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$ with central angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$.
Find the exact area.

options.why: Forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in the annular sector area formula.
Subtracted the radii before squaring: $\frac{1}{2}(10-6)^2\theta$.
Calculated only the outer sector area and doubled it.

questions.question_text:
A sector has an area of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^{2}$ and an arc length of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ cm}$.
What are the exact values of $r$ and $\theta$?

options.why: Forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in $A = \frac{1}{2}rl$.
Used $A=\tfrac{1}{4}rl$ instead of $A=\tfrac{1}{2}rl$, giving $r=4A/l=8\text{ cm}$, then used $\theta=l/r$.
Equated the angle directly to the arc length.

questions.question_text:
A sector subtending $60^{\circ}$ is cut from a circle of radius $3\text{ cm}$.
What is the exact area of the remaining sector?

options.why: Calculated the area of the removed sector instead of the remaining sector.
Calculated the whole circle area without subtracting the removed sector.
Used the remaining angle $5\pi/3$ but omitted the factor of $1/2$ in the sector area formula.

questions.solution_text:
The remaining angle is $300^{\circ}=\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.
$A=\tfrac{1}{2}(3^{2})\dfrac{5\pi}{3}=\dfrac{15\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text:
A garden is composed of an isosceles triangle $\Delta ABD$ with $AB = AD = 6\text{ m}$ and $\angle DAB = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$, and a sector $BCD$ with centre $B$, radii $BD$ and $BC$, and central angle $\angle DBC = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$. The sector lies on the opposite side of $BD$ from $A$.
What is the exact area of the garden?

options.why: Used $r = 6$ instead of $r = BD = \sqrt{108}$ for the sector radius.
Forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in the triangle area formula.
Calculated only the sector area and omitted the triangle.

questions.solution_text:
Cosine rule in $\Delta ABD$:
$BD^{2} = 6^{2} + 6^{2} - 2(6)(6)\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = 36 + 36 + 36 = 108$
$A_{\Delta ABD} = \tfrac{1}{2}(6)(6)\sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = 9\sqrt{3}\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_{\text{sector}} = \tfrac{1}{2}(108)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 18\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$\text{Total Area} = 9\sqrt{3} + 18\pi\text{ m}^{2}$

questions.question_text:
A circle has radius $8\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$. A chord subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$.
What is the exact perimeter of the minor segment?

options.why: Added two radii instead of the chord.
Used $\pi$ instead of $\pi/2$ when calculating the arc length.
Calculated only the arc length and omitted the chord.

questions.solution_text:
$l=r\theta=8\sqrt{2}\times\dfrac{\pi}{2}=4\sqrt{2}\pi\text{ cm}$
By cosine rule:
$c^{2}=(8\sqrt{2})^{2}+(8\sqrt{2})^{2}-2(8\sqrt{2})^{2}\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}=256$
$c=16\text{ cm}$
$P=l+c=4\sqrt{2}\pi+16\text{ cm}$
